item.research_question: How does the Direct Energy Deposition (DED) process affect the phase formation, microstructure, hardness, and thermal properties of Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al refractory high-entropy alloys compared to thermodynamic predictions?
item.material_system: Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al refractory high-entropy alloy (powders mixed at equal ratios to the phase analysis design), deposited on Ti-6Al-4V and Inconel 718 substrates
item.processing_route: Direct Energy Deposition (DED) using a high-power diode laser (1000 W max, 780 W used), 980 nm wavelength, 3 mm spot size, 40% hatch overlap, 2 layers to 1 mm thickness, room temperature, sealed environment with Ar shield gas and N carrier gas
item.test_conditions: Microhardness measured via Vickers (9 indentations per area); Heat-Affected Zone (HAZ) analyzed via preheating test (500 W laser, 15 L/min Ar, 3 s duration); Microstructure analyzed via SEM, EBSD, XRD, and EDS
key_findings: The actual microstructure contained sigma (σ), BCC A2, and Ti2Ni phases, differing from the predicted BCC A2, BCC B2, and Laves phases.
EBSD analysis revealed phase fractions of 64.2% σ phase, 28.2% BCC A2 phase, and 7.6% Ti2Ni phase.
The grain size of the deposited alloy was 1–35 μm, which is finer than the 45–150 μm powder size used.
The microhardness of the deposited Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al was measured to be approximately 900 HV.
The microhardness of the Ti-6Al-4V and Inconel 718 substrates increased by 17–19% compared to wrought material due to heat treatment effects.
The HAZ depth of Ti-6Al-4V was reduced by 16.07% and Inconel 718 by 14.42% after deposition of the RHEA.
The σ phase peak intensity in XRD analysis was higher than those of the BCC A2 and Ti2Ni phases.
item.mechanism: The microstructure growth and fine grain size are attributed to the high energy density of the laser in DED, which rapidly increases temperature and then causes rapid cooling, acting as a heat treatment effect. The high thermal diffusivity of the Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al alloy reduces the heat-affected zone. The high hardness is related to the high volume fraction of the brittle σ phase.
item.limitations: The accuracy of the phase analysis is highly dependent on the thermodynamic database used, and a complete thermodynamic analysis of each binary and ternary phase diagram belonging to the multicomponent system was not performed. XRD analysis generated significant noise caused by unmelted powder inside the deposited material.
item.future_work: The authors propose to analyze the effect of each process variable on phase formation and find suitable manufacturing conditions for RHEAs by controlling the process variables.
quotes: The microstructure of Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al showed that the BCC A2 phase, which grew first at high temperatures, grew first, and then the σ phase grew rapidly before the Ti2Ni precipitated phase grew.
The microhardness of the Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al deposited area was measured to be approximately 900 HV.
The HAZ decreased, owing to the high thermal diffusivity of Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al.
